results.summary_before: This is a one-tile demoscene entry that generates animated graphics for a VGA monitor while racing the beam, using mathematical functions to produce the imagery. It also outputs mono audio on a bidirectional pin, and the whole sequence repeats after about 68 seconds. It needs a 25 MHz clock, a reset, a Tiny VGA PMOD for the display and a TT Audio PMOD for sound. The design is notable as a competition submission in the 1-tile category and relies on standard Tiny Tapeout VGA and audio pinouts.

results.summary_before: This is a single-ended two-stage Miller-compensated operational transconductance amplifier with a self-biasing beta-multiplier current reference and configurable compensation, fabricated in SKY 130nm. The non-inverting and inverting inputs and the output are on analog pins, while two select pins configure the compensation and a beat output is provided. It is intended to be operated in feedback, for example as a unity-gain buffer by tying the inverting input to the output, from which the gain-bandwidth product can be estimated. The documentation is concise but clearly describes the circuit and a basic test configuration.

results.summary_before: This is a low-dropout linear regulator that accepts 1.2 V to 3 V on an analog input pin and produces a regulated 1 V output at up to 50 mA. A 0.6 V reference is applied on a separate analog pin, and the output appears on another analog pin. The documentation lists expected characteristics including 0.2 V dropout, 82 percent efficiency at 1.2 V input, 6.78 mV/V line regulation and 67 mV/A load regulation, along with schematic and layout images. Testing is simply a matter of connecting the input voltage and the 0.6 V reference and measuring the output.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-wire DC continuity tester for Ethernet cables, driving each wire in turn and reporting per-wire pass/fail on eight LEDs. It requires a far-end shorting plug that ties all wires together and a near-end board with series resistors, pull-downs, and TVS diodes for protection. The chip continuously retests, allowing intermittent faults to be observed as flickering LEDs. It is a practical test tool rather than a data communication device, and its operation is well documented.

results.summary_before: Missile Command is a tiny version of Atari's classic game, implemented in Verilog for Tiny Tapeout. It uses a VGA PMOD for video and a GamePad PMOD for control, supporting a single player. The game features missiles, bombs, explosions, a fortress, and level progression, with sprites generated by formulas or predefined matrices. It requires external hardware including a TinyTapeout dev kit, VGA PMOD, GamePad PMOD, monitor, and SNES controller, and is notable for being a complete game implementation on a 2x2 tile footprint.

results.summary_before: HSXO wraps a high-speed crystal oscillator IP block from Chipalooza 2024 into the Tiny Tapeout analog template. It forms a Pierce oscillator when a passive crystal is bridged between XIN and XOUT with load capacitors to ground, and it needs a 1 uA bias current on IBIAS plus ENA high and STDBY low. A clock appears on DOUT after a start-up delay, and XIN and XOUT can be probed while accounting for probe loading. The block could theoretically support 4 to 16 MHz crystals, but the higher end needs shorter traces than the demo board provides.
